card.name: Words before a drug's pharmacokinetic detail
card.fires_on: Small connecting words (its, cross, is) or a blank gap right after a drug name or its verb, where a pharmacokinetic fact follows, such as metabolism, placental transfer, elimination or bioavailability.

modes.label: Its before metabolism
modes.description: The word "its" after "inhibits" in valproate interaction text, just before hepatic metabolism.
modes.example: Valproate displaces phenytoin from its plasma albumin binding sites and inhibits<< its>> hepatic metabolism.

modes.label: Verb after drug name
modes.description: A verb like "cross" or "is" directly after a drug or drug class, leading into placental transfer or elimination route.
modes.example: Thiazides<< cross>> the placental barrier and appear in cord

modes.label: Gap in radiotracer or bioavailability text
modes.description: A blank or letter spot inside Fluorodopa F 18 names or just before a bioavailability percentage.
modes.example: Fluorodopa<< F>> 18 PET scans are interpreted visually

card.writes: Little clear effect; it weakly suppresses words like targeting, targeted and delivery.
card.plain: It fires on the small word right after a drug name when the sentence is about how the body handles that drug.
